summary: A star is a light in the night sky. Stars that defy counting illustrate the promise to Abraham. Their light and position also supply images for people and rulers.

senses.definition: God makes the stars and sets them in the heavens. Psalm 8 places the stars beside the moon as works of his fingers. The psalmist marvels that their maker also attends to human beings.

senses.gloss: stars as a measure of multitude
senses.definition: Abraham is asked to count the stars and is promised offspring as numerous. The comparison recurs when the promise is repeated to Isaac.

senses.gloss: star as an image of a ruler or person
senses.definition: Joseph sees eleven stars bow to him in a dream. Balaam sets a star rising from Jacob beside a sceptre from Israel. Daniel compares those who lead many to righteousness with shining stars.
The travellers from the east see a star and follow it. Paul compares the differing brightness of stars, and Hebrews recalls the promise of descendants as numerous as the stars.

note: The Syriac word is indexed under כוכב. The received Hebrew noun supplies the evidence for star. A Hebrew verb meaning shine or roll cannot be established from its use.
